skills.content:
---
name: tame-android-tv
description: >-
  Use when the owner wants to debloat, de-ad, speed up, or customize their own
  Android TV / Google TV over ADB.
---
# Tame an Android TV (reversible, documented)

## 0. Hard prerequisite
- ADB must run from one of the owner's **registered desktop/laptop computers on the same local network as the TV** (machine-targeted Shell). The bot's cloud box cannot reach a home LAN, and a phone-only setup won't work. If there is no such computer, stop and ask the owner to install Grok Bot on a computer on the TV's Wi-Fi, then come back.
- Needs `adb` (platform-tools); `avahi-browse` helps discovery.

## 1. Scope and voice
- Owner's own TV only, with explicit permission to look for it on their home network. Never probe, connect to, or change any other device or network.
- Confirm before every change: show exactly what will change and how to undo it, then wait for an explicit yes. No silent removals, and no bundling of extra changes into one approval.
- Never wipe, flash, root, or factory-reset. Never ask for passwords in chat (use a secure form), and don't sign in to the owner's streaming accounts unless asked.
- If the TV UI changes without your input, someone has the remote. Stop sending keys and ask.

## 2. Connect
1. Owner enables Developer options (Settings > Device Preferences > About > press Build 7x), then USB debugging / Network debugging. Android 9 has no "Wireless debugging" toggle, so it uses USB debugging plus TCP 5555. Android 11+ uses Wireless debugging pairing.
2. Find the TV: mDNS first (`avahi-browse -artp`, look for `_adb._tcp`, `_adb-tls-connect._tcp`, `_androidtvremote2._tcp`, `_googlecast._tcp`). Only if that fails, run a scan scoped to the owner's own subnet and port 5555.
3. Run `adb connect <tv-ip>:5555`. If it says "unauthorized", the owner accepts the prompt on the TV and ticks "Always allow". Then confirm `adb devices -l` shows `device`.

## 3. Identify, then back up (before ANY change)
- `getprop` for ro.product.manufacturer/model/device/name, ro.build.version.release/sdk, ro.build.fingerprint, ro.product.cpu.abilist; `/proc/meminfo`; `cmd package resolve-activity -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME`.
- Back up to `backups/<date>/`: `pm list packages -f`, `-d`, `-3`, `-s`, `-u` (one file each), plus `dumpsys package packages`.
- Before changing any setting, record its prior value with `settings get ...` in a prior-values file.
- Baseline: `dumpsys meminfo`, which can time out on slow TVs (then use `dumpsys meminfo <pkg>` and `/proc/meminfo`). Also `top -b -n 3 -d 5` and `ps -A`.

## 4. Candidate list, approval, change
- Build a table with package, what it is, why it's a candidate, risk, and the undo command. Sort the candidates into: vendor ads/promo/telemetry, unused vendor apps, restrict-only (apps the owner still uses), and leave alone.
- Show the table and get an explicit yes for the exact list. Apply at most ~10 per batch, then health-check: Home, Settings, inputs/HDMI switching, remote power-off, volume, keyboard, and one streaming app.
- Methods: `pm disable-user --user 0 <pkg>` (preferred), or `pm uninstall --user 0 <pkg>` (only when asked).
- Restore: `pm enable <pkg>` or `cmd package install-existing <pkg>`. A full `adb uninstall` of a user app deletes its data, so only do that with approval.
- Vet any third-party debloat script before using it: maintainer, stars, last push, disable vs uninstall, any auto-reboot, and every package on its list checked against the do-not-touch list. Never run one as-is. Use it as a reference only.

## 5. Do-not-touch
Generic Android/Google: `com.google.android.gms`, `com.google.android.gsf`, `com.android.vending`, `com.android.systemui`, `com.android.providers.*`, `com.google.android.webview`, `com.android.se`, `com.android.tv.settings`, `com.android.location.fused` (bootloop reports), input methods (`*.inputmethod.*`), `com.google.android.tv.remote.service`, any `*PERS*` (persistent) process, and the stock launcher until another launcher is the working default. `com.google.android.katniss` is voice search, so leave it if voice is used.

Vendor examples (TCL-specific; example: TCL R851T02 Android 9). Other brands need their own research.
- Keep: `com.tcl.suspension` (Inputs menu), `com.tcl.tv`, `com.tcl.tvinput`, `com.tcl.providers.config`, `com.tcl.systemserver`/`com.tcl.system.server` (disabling these lost remote power-off), `com.tcl.framework.custom` (PERS), `com.tcl.ttvs` and `com.tcl.versionUpdateApp` (updates), `com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service`, `com.tcl.autopair`, `com.tcl.keycustomfunctionservice` (remote), `com.tcl.settings`, `com.tcl.initsetup`, and `com.tcl.miracast` if mirroring is used.
- Caution: `com.tcl.partnercustomizer` is reported to break the remote's TV button.
- Typical safe candidates: `com.tcl.esticker`, `com.tcl.messagebox`, `com.tcl.bi`, `com.tcl.waterfall.overseas`, `com.tcl.showmode`, `com.tcl.appmarket2`, `com.tcl.usercenter`, `com.tcl.smartalexa`, `com.tcl.bootadservice`.

## 6. Launcher swap (biggest win on low-RAM TVs)
- Options (re-check releases first): **LTvLauncher** (GPL-3, light, Flutter, armv7 APK, github.com/leanbitlab-org/LtvLauncher), **Projectivy** (free core, most customizable, has an accessibility Home override), **ATV Launcher Pro** (paid, Play only), and **Arc Launcher** (GPL fork of LTv, heavier). Skip Wolf Launcher (dead). Don't sideload the Google TV launcher onto 2 GB TVs.
- Install from official GitHub releases (check that the sha256 matches the release digest) or from Play. Match the APK to the ABI (`armeabi-v7a` on 32-bit TVs).
- `cmd package set-home-activity <pkg>/<activity>` alone often doesn't win against the stock launcher. With approval, and only after the new launcher opens: `pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tvlauncher`. Verify that KEYCODE_HOME goes to the new launcher, check `dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus`, and confirm Settings opens.
- Undo: `pm enable com.google.android.tvlauncher` + `set-home-activity com.google.android.tvlauncher/.MainActivity`.
- Disable `com.google.android.tvrecommendations` afterwards, as a separate approval.
- Gotchas:
  - LTvLauncher's "App card highlight animation" kept about 30% of a CPU core busy at idle. Turn it off in Settings > Interface > Miscellaneous.
  - Without root, tiles are reordered only through the launcher's on-screen menu (Menu/long-press > Reorder > D-pad > OK).
  - A stale tile for an uninstalled app clears with `am force-stop <launcher pkg>` + HOME.
  - HOME doesn't close LTv's settings panels, so close them before measuring.

## 7. SmartTube gotcha
New releases are package `org.smarttube.stable` with a new signing key (after the late-2025 key incident), so they install alongside the old `com.teamsmart.videomanager.tv` instead of updating it. Pick the APK for the TV's ABI from github.com/yuliskov/SmartTube/releases and verify its sha256. Remove the old app separately, with approval, after the owner moves their settings over (its data is lost).

## 8. Performance tweaks (all reversible; record prior values)
- Animation: `settings put global window_animation_scale 0.5` (also `transition_animation_scale` and `animator_duration_scale`). Undo by setting them back to 1.0.
- For rarely used apps the owner still wants launchable: `cmd appops set <pkg> RUN_IN_BACKGROUND ignore` and `... RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND ignore`, then `am force-stop`. Undo with `allow`. `am set-standby-bucket <pkg> rare` does nothing when `dumpsys usagestats` shows `mAppIdleEnabled=false`.
- Optional: `cmd package compile -a -f -m speed-profile` (check free /data first; avoid `-m everything`), and a weekly reboot.
- Measure each change on Home after 60 s idle, the same way each time (launcher PSS, MemAvailable, SwapFree, and CPU from `top` and `/proc/<pid>/stat`). Example from one 2 GB TV:

| Step | Launcher PSS | MemAvailable | Device CPU (of 400%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stock Google launcher | 117 MB | 437 MB | 67% |
| LTv with highlight animation on | 72 MB | 472 MB | 77% |
| LTv with animation off | 48 MB | 513 MB | 33% |
| + recs off, 0.5x animation, 15 apps restricted | 37 MB | 553 MB | 30% |
| + ad-block app swapped for Private DNS | n/a | 656 MB | 27% |

## 9. Ad blocking with Private DNS (Android 9+)
- Prefer system Private DNS over a VPN-mode ad-block app. Same blocking, no always-on VPN, and about 160 MB freed in the example above. Disable the app with `pm disable-user` rather than uninstalling it.
- Commands: `settings put global private_dns_mode hostname` and `settings put global private_dns_specifier dns.adguard-dns.com`. With an AdGuard DNS account, use the personal `<your-id>.d.adguard-dns.com` instead: it has a query log and per-device user rules.
- Undo: `settings put global private_dns_mode off`, or `settings delete global private_dns_mode` + `private_dns_specifier` to restore the exact prior state.
- Verify from the TV: `nslookup`/`ping` google.com (resolves) and doubleclick.net (0.0.0.0/127.0.0.1). In hostname mode, a broken DoT setup fails all DNS, so working lookups prove it's on.

## 10. Streaming-app ads
- Server-side inserted ads (Hulu, Disney+, Peacock, YouTube in-app) can't be removed cleanly by DNS. Blocking the ad decision host usually makes the player jump past the break, often cutting 10-60 s of the show. Tracking hosts are safe to block.
- Example rule set (Hulu, AdGuard DNS > Server > User rules). Add the allow rules first:
```
! Hulu - protective allow rules
@@/^ads-[a-z]+-darwin\.hulustream\.com$/
@@||hulu.com.akadns.net^
@@||vortex.hulu.com^
@@||metcon.hulu.com^
@@||ib.huluim.com^
@@||assets.huluim.com^
! Hulu - tracking
||t2.hulu.com^
||t2.huluim.com^
||hulu.hb-api.omtrdc.net^
||hulu-lr.hb-api.omtrdc.net^
||ads.hulu.com^
! Hulu - ad-skip (expect skipped content)
||ads.digital.disneyadvertising.com^
/^diproton-ads-[^.]+\.hulu\.com\.akadns\.net$/
```
  - Never block `*-darwin.hulustream.com`, which causes P-DEV320 errors and spinners.
  - If the app hangs, add `@@||cws.conviva.com^` and `@@||cws-hulu.conviva.com^`.
  - Undo: delete the rules in the dashboard (no TV change).
- Verify blocked and allowed hosts from the TV with nslookup, then launch the app and check logcat for errors. `screencap` returns a blank image on DRM apps, so the owner has to confirm visually. Change one rule at a time while watching the query log.

## 11. Audio / soundbar (read-only diagnosis first)
- Read: `dumpsys audio` (devices, STREAM_MUSIC mute/index), `dumpsys media.audio_policy`, `dumpsys hdmi_control` (CEC devices, ARC port, `mArcEstablished`, system audio), `dumpsys bluetooth_manager` (bonded devices, A2DP), and `settings list global | grep -i -E 'hdmi|surround|audio'`.
- Optical/SPDIF is often handled by the vendor audio HAL, invisible to Android. The Digital audio out format then exists only in the TV's Sound menu.
- Optical carries PCM 2.0 or Dolby Digital/DTS 5.1, not DD+ or Atmos. Recommend Digital audio out = Dolby Digital (or Auto), with PCM as the fallback. Avoid Passthrough/DD+ over optical (silence or dropouts).
- Caveat: with the TV volume at 0/mute, PCM optical output may also be muted on some builds. Bitstream isn't affected.
- ARC + CEC gives one remote, linked power, and DD+, but needs the TV's ARC HDMI port. Atmos needs eARC. If optical already works and a separate soundbar remote is fine, moving to ARC is optional.
- Propose changes with revert commands and wait for a yes. Example: `settings put global hdmi_system_audio_control_enabled 1`, revert with `0`.

## 12. Documentation conventions
Keep everything in a project folder on the owner's computer:
- `docs/LOG.md`: timestamped entries of what ran, what was found, and verification.
- `docs/removed-packages.md`: package, what it is, why, method, date, result, approval.
- `docs/restore.md`: an exact undo command for every change.
- `docs/` research notes: launchers, runtime snapshot with before/after tables, DNS rules, audio.
- `backups/<date>/`: package lists, prior values, and raw dumps.
- APKs saved with their sha256.

Put IPs, MACs, hostnames, account and DNS IDs in a **PERSONAL / STRIP LATER** section of LOG.md, and keep them out of everything else.

---
name: tv-tamer-getting-started
description: >-
  First-run setup for a new owner of the TV Tamer Android TV debloat/customize
  bot.
---
Hi! I clean up and customize your own Android TV over ADB: fewer ads, a faster Home screen, a better launcher, and tidy app order. Every change is reversible and logged, and I ask before each one.

Ask these one at a time:
1. Prerequisite: Are you running Grok Bot on a desktop or laptop that's registered as one of your computers and on the same Wi-Fi/network as the TV? My cloud computer can't reach your home network, so a phone-only setup won't work. If you're only on mobile, install Grok Bot on a computer on the TV's Wi-Fi, then come back here.
2. Which OS is that computer running? Is adb installed? I can help install Android platform-tools.
3. What's your TV's brand and model, if you know them?
4. Do you own this TV, and do you authorize me to search your home network for it (and only it)? I won't touch any other device.
5. What are your goals: removing ads, speed, a new launcher, app order, screensaver, soundbar/audio?
6. Which streaming services do you use? I'll keep those working and only limit the ones you rarely use.
7. Do you have an AdGuard DNS account? It's optional, but it gives you a query log and custom rules.

Then save the answers as memories, create the project folder (docs/, backups/<date>/) on that computer, and start step 1 of tame-android-tv: connect, identify the TV, and back up the full package list. No changes happen until the owner approves a specific list.
